channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Strengthens Counter-Terrorism Cooperation Amidst Globalization Challenges
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Interior Minister attended international events in China focusing on combating terrorism, extremism, and transnational crime. The conference emphasized the global nature of these threats and the need for enhanced international cooperation. Participants discussed new security challenges and the importance of digital methods for crime prevention and counteraction.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Defendant in Power Seizure Case Requests Open Trial from President
item.description: Temirlan Sultanbekov, on trial for an alleged attempt to seize power, has appealed to President Sadyr Japarov for a public trial. Having spent significant time in detention, he argues an open trial would demonstrate the fairness of the investigation and judicial process. He states he seeks nothing for himself, only justice.

item.title: Over 96,000 Uzbek Citizens Returned from Russia in 10 Days
item.description: More than 96,000 Uzbek citizens have returned to Uzbekistan from Russia in the past 10 days. Over 54,000 came directly from Russia, while the rest transited through Kazakhstan. Assistance was provided to citizens facing difficult situations.

item.title: All Uzbek school textbooks to transition to new alphabet by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to fully transition all school textbooks to the updated Uzbek alphabet between 2027 and 2031. The Deputy Minister of Preschool and School Education stated that textbooks for first graders will use the new alphabet starting in 2027, with all textbooks updated by 2031.

item.title: Five arrested at Namangan airport attempting to smuggle gold worth $1.1 billion to India
item.description: Five individuals were apprehended at Namangan International Airport for attempting to illegally export gold worth 1.1 billion soums to India. The suspects, from Andijan and Fergana regions, were using their bodies as 'live containers' to smuggle 555 grams of gold bars and 200 grams of jewelry.

item.title: Uzbek Senate Approves New 28-Letter Latin-Based Alphabet Variant
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan approved a new variant of the Latin-based Uzbek alphabet, consisting of 28 letters and one apostrophe, replacing the current 26 letters and three digraphs. The proposed reform aims to align the writing system with the "one sound - one letter" principle and address issues with digital usage. The bill now moves to the president for review.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Showcases First Robotic Surgery System at Medical Academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's first robotic surgery system was unveiled at the Kyrgyz State Medical Academy. The Ministry of Health reported that the robot assists surgeons by enabling precise instrument control and magnified views through small incisions, enhancing complex operations.

item.title: UzAuto Motors Launches First Chevrolet Hybrid Model, the Equinox PHEV
item.description: UzAuto Motors has announced the launch of its first hybrid model, the Chevrolet Equinox PHEV crossover. Available in two trims, the vehicle features a plug-in hybrid system allowing short trips on electric power alone, with a total range exceeding 1000 km.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election Date Set for January 27, 2027, Parliament to Confirm
item.description: The Zhogorku Kenesh (parliament) is expected to officially set the presidential election date for January 27, 2027, on September 24. The Central Election Commission stated that the election will proceed on this date regardless of parliamentary resolution, with campaigning to begin in December.

item.title: GKNB uncovers state damage in purchase of two combine harvesters in Naryn region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Committee for National Security (GKNB) has identified state damage amounting to 4.945 million soms during the procurement of two combine harvesters in the Min-Bulak rural district of Naryn region. Criminal proceedings are underway to investigate the actions of involved officials and recover the losses.

item.title: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov writes letter to Kyrgyzstan's president
item.description: Imprisoned politician Temirlan Sultanbekov has written a letter to President Sadyr Japarov from pre-trial detention center SIZO-1. Sultanbekov stated he would not ask for mercy, emphasizing his commitment to the 'Kyrgyz spirit,' and requested an open trial.

item.title: Russian scientists to study infections in Kyrgyzstan with population surveys
item.description: The St. Petersburg Pasteur Research Institute will organize population studies in Kyrgyzstan from October 16 to November 15, 2026. The research aims to study infections, involving the collection and laboratory testing of biological samples from 70 points across the country.

item.title: Sughd region plans to process waste into organic fertilizers
item.description: Officials in Tajikistan's Sughd region met with Iranian counterparts to discuss cooperation in waste management and recycling. Plans include updating sewage networks, reconstructing landfills, and implementing technologies to produce organic fertilizers from waste, potentially starting in Khujand.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Housing Market Sees 21% Growth in Seven Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's housing market experienced a 21% increase in sales during the first seven months of the year. The number of real estate transactions rose to 34,300. Sales growth was observed in most regions, with the highest figures recorded in the capital city.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan introduces first robotic surgical system at medical academy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Medical Academy has unveiled the country's first robotic surgical system. The system enhances surgeon precision and visualization through small incisions, but the doctor remains in full control during operations. The academy plans to begin robot-assisted surgeries soon, with another system to be acquired for the National Center for Mother and Child Healthcare.

item.title: Two former police officers in Syrdarya sentenced to 5 and 6 years for bribery
item.description: Two former officers from the Khovos district police department in Syrdarya region were sentenced to five and six years in prison for demanding bribes. They were accused of fabricating evidence and extorting money from a farmer regarding a land dispute. The officers were apprehended while receiving part of the demanded sum.

item.title: Uzbek citizens returning from abroad can receive grants up to 60 million soums for business expansion
item.description: Uzbek citizens who worked abroad and returned to start businesses can receive grants up to 60 million soums to expand their ventures and create jobs. The program, a collaboration between the Migration Agency and IOM with Swedish funding, targets returnees from 2025-2026. Special support is given to women entrepreneurs.

item.title: Chinese Vice Premier Calls for Greater Openness in Services Trade
item.description: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang emphasized the need for greater openness and cooperation in the services trade sector, stating it's a global necessity. He proposed reducing barriers to cross-border factor movement and promoting liberalization to support socio-economic development.

item.title: Tajikistan Celebrates 35th Anniversary of Independence with Cultural Program
item.description: Dushanbe hosted a cultural program at the National Stadium to mark Tajikistan's 35th anniversary of independence. President Emomali Rahmon addressed the attendees, highlighting the importance of peace, stability, and national unity for the country's development and prosperity.

item.title: Parents of Children with SSPE Protest for Medical Aid and Support
item.description: Parents of children suffering from Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE), a severe complication of measles, gathered outside the Ministry of Health in Uzbekistan demanding essential medications, medical care, and financial assistance. The ministry reported approximately 350 children have SSPE, with 60 deaths.

item.title: Counterfeit $8,400 in Tashkent Seized; Suspects Arrested
item.description: Individuals attempting to exchange counterfeit $8,400 for genuine currency have been apprehended in Tashkent. The fake money was reportedly supplied from Turkey. A criminal case has been initiated against those involved in circulating the counterfeit bills.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares for fish exports to Russia using local feed
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is undergoing certification procedures to ensure uninterrupted fish exports to Russia, using domestically produced feed. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture and Processing Industry reported this. The move aims to support local producers and reduce reliance on foreign supplies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament to Consider Presidential Election Date on September 24
item.description: The Jogorku Kenesh will review the presidential election appointment on September 24, according to the head of the Central Election Commission. The elections are scheduled for January 27, 2027. Previously, a September 17 date was considered. The election will proceed even if parliament fails to adopt a resolution.

item.title: Sirdaryo Kindergarten Head Fined for Forcing Staff to Collect Votes
item.description: A kindergarten director in Sirdaryo region was fined for compelling staff into forced labor, including cleaning and soliciting votes for an 'Open Budget' initiative. The Ombudsman confirmed violations of the Labor Code. The director faces a fine exceeding 20 million UZS. Such projects will be removed from the budget initiative.

item.title: US Destroys Five Iranian Tankers in Response to Warship Attack
item.description: The US Central Command destroyed five Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Hark Island in retaliation for Iran's repeated missile attacks on a US Navy warship. The warship evaded the attacks, and no US personnel were harmed. Iran claimed successful strikes on US destroyers and a Jordanian airbase.

item.title: Solar power plant developer overcharged by nearly 24 million soms
item.description: A company in Kyrgyzstan, granted 800 hectares for a solar power plant, was overcharged compensation payments by over 23.9 million soms, according to the Prosecutor General's Office. The overcharge resulted from an unjustified coefficient applied during calculations for agricultural production losses. Disciplinary action was taken against officials.

item.title: Donald Trump: Vladimir Putin is ready for a deal on Ukraine
item.description: US President Donald Trump stated that Russian leader Vladimir Putin is ready to conclude a peace deal with Ukraine. He told Fox News that Putin wants a deal and it would be good if Zelensky also wanted one. Trump mentioned that Putin and Zelensky 'hate each other,' hindering agreement. He also suggested a bilateral meeting with Putin could happen.

item.title: Uzbekistan to consolidate work of local authorities, banks under deputy prime minister
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to hold weekly meetings chaired by the Deputy Prime Minister for work with mahallas to discuss issues related to their activities. A new position, Deputy Prime Minister and Chairman of the Association of Uzbek Mahallas, has been established and filled. This official will coordinate the work of local authorities, district organizations, and banks.

item.title: Uzbekistan Significantly Reduces Poverty Rates Ahead of Schedule
item.description: Uzbekistan is reducing poverty faster than projected, with the poverty rate falling from 17% in 2021 to an estimated 4.5% by 2026. This decline is attributed to job creation, entrepreneurship support, and increased use of household plots for income, alongside reduced inequality.

item.title: Bukhara Region and USA Expand Economic and Tourism Ties
item.description: The Bukhara region of Uzbekistan and the United States are strengthening economic and tourism cooperation. Discussions between the regional governor and the US deputy ambassador focused on investment potential, economic opportunities, tourism resources, and ongoing joint projects in agriculture and education.

item.title: Uzbekistan President Reviews Employment and Income Growth Initiatives
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev critically reviewed regional efforts to boost employment and increase public income. A new system assigns regional and district-level responsibilities to khokims, with employment agencies and economic structures tasked with local job creation and income enhancement. Some officials were noted for failing to engage directly with communities and businesses.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Regulate Illegally Occupied Land Around Apartment Buildings
item.description: Uzbekistan may offer land plots for private kindergartens, schools, and technical schools at a starting price of 1 million soums for auction if entrepreneurs commit to educating children from needy families for free. This initiative aims to provide employment for parents and quality education for children.

item.title: Building Valued at $1.2 Million Returned to State Ownership in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A building and a 23,500 square meter land plot in Naryn, Kyrgyzstan, valued at approximately 96.5 million soms (about $1.2 million), have been returned to state ownership. The property was illegally transferred to private hands in 2003 by officials violating land legislation.

item.title: Canada Imposes 50% Tariffs on US Goods in Response to US Trade Measures
item.description: Canada has imposed tariffs of up to 50% on US products starting September 8, retaliating against US President Donald Trump's administration's decision to levy 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The measures cover approximately CAD 27.6 billion in imports and include steel, aluminum, dairy, and electronics.

item.title: Uzbekistan's growing international interest highlighted by foreign media
item.description: Foreign media partners have focused on Uzbekistan's developments, including economic activity, tourism, and digital transformation. Publications from Anadolu and TASS noted the establishment of a strategic partnership between Uzbekistan and Serbia, with leaders signing a joint declaration and agreements on cooperation in agriculture, tourism, and culture.

item.title: SCO cooperation in AI can shape a shared digital future, referencing Al-Khwarizmi
item.description: The Bishkek Declaration calls for safe and responsible AI use, ensuring it does not harm human life or undermine state sovereignty. Uzbekistan's IT Park representative highlighted the region's historical connection to AI through mathematician Al-Khwarizmi, whose work on algorithms is foundational to modern AI development.

item.title: Uzbekistan may allow first-floor apartments for business without reclassification
item.description: Uzbekistan proposes allowing the use of first-floor apartments in multi-story buildings for commercial purposes without reclassifying them as non-residential. This aims to facilitate small businesses like shops and service centers, simplifying the current complex process of obtaining permits.

item.title: SCO summit in Bishkek expands agenda beyond security to economic cooperation
item.description: The 25th anniversary Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek marked a significant milestone, expanding its focus beyond traditional security issues. Discussions included trade, economic cooperation, investment, transport, energy, digitalization, and artificial intelligence, reflecting a comprehensive approach to Eurasian development. The summit reaffirmed the 'Shanghai Spirit' of mutual trust and consensus.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing its country application for support from the Global Alliance on Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A GAVI mission visited Bishkek for a working group meeting on the application, attended by health officials and representatives from WHO and UNICEF.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares application for Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization support
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is preparing a country application for support from the Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization (GAVI) for the 2026-2030 period. A working group meeting, attended by health officials and international partners, discussed the application for GAVI 6.0 funding.
